title: Hands for the Strips

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The seed goes in by the fist and the hands go in by the look. Ask either what it cost and it will tell you the weather.
epigraph.attribution: A planting saying of Low Kiln

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-four-to-one-hundred-and-six-day-old body carried everywhere; the old life colours the noticing (the exact count kept against a house that keeps it badly, the hand to the record before the hand to the person, a fist of seed read as the ninety-second sorting, an anatomy read perfectly and worth nothing) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, Waiting Room or collector interior

scenes.title: The Hands Go In
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 104, Seed 15, Fifthday, morning in the worked strips east of Low Kiln and the Clay Yard; the boy carried at the edge. The hands the strips wanted for a month at last go in: bodies stoop in the worked brown ground, seed comes out of fists in handfuls that nobody counts, brooms go around what the sweep left, and the work is done with a glance and a count of handfuls and no figure spoken anywhere. A woman counts seed into a fist and will not say what the fist holds; a man standing with the barrow nearly speaks the number of hands and thinks better of it, so the withholding becomes an act done in the planting itself. Sella Vail gives the instruction to the bucket and the broom before anybody and never to the basket, keeps her half-pace from every open slate, and says the house where another woman would say I. Berr Clay comes down from the north road with the red wool cord of his office folded under his coat, wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, reads one in twelve as the notice says, says a number goes into a slate and not into a strip and that the levy is called and not by him, and goes off with the box in his house locked and the true subtraction inside. The boy, one hundred and four days old and told by nobody, sets the direction he has carried for a month beside the number the yard will not give and does not join them; he reads a fist of seed as the ninety-second sorting of twenty bodies, an exact clean reading worth nothing to a body that cannot lift a hand to its own chin. Meaningful change: the direction becomes worked ground with hands in it, still counted in glances and handfuls and never in a figure. Advances T071/T072 (104), T077, T058/T079, T009/T013/T092, T041/T047. Withheld: no figure for hands or strips, no joining of direction and number, no ending.

scenes.title: Two Rooms That Do Not Touch
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry continued, Day 104, Seed 15, afternoon and going of the light at the loaf shelf in the Vail kiln-house and on the bed under the roof. A neighbour reaching past the bare board speaks again of the old space at the loaf row's end as a thing that came in with the planting, her hand to the board before her eyes to the boy, and goes with her pot; the boy files the saying beside the one T097 already waits on, planted and not paid, and keeps the shelf's two unnamed gaps in the next room from touching the fold's one stiff crust and its unnamed empty place. Sella Vail moves her lips along the loaf row and gives the house no figure, glances at the clay jar on the wall shelf, touches the widow's mark at no hour because a shelf, a strip and a bed are not openings, and tells the fire it is the thaw; the fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and four days. The new finer grey lies unswept beside the clean dark line and is called the thaw, and the space under the lowest rack is gone around as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it and entered by nobody. Dusk: she carries him up at the half-pace from every open slate, sets him on his bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread at his mouth frozen. The river's note comes through the finger's-width-open door from the Ilm and the kiln's four, four and a gap through the floor, in two separate places; he is one hundred and four days old and nobody has told him so. Advances T060/T086, T097 (advanced, not paid), T071/T072 (104), T058/T079, T088, T009/T013/T092, T061/T082. Withheld: no joining of the two rooms, no third gap, no name, no payment.

scenes.title: The Bite That Holds and Takes
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 105, Seed 16, Sixthday, before first grey through midday at the Vail wheel-shed and its damper, under the Vail roof at dusk. Men have come in before first grey and spoken low in the finger's-width-open back room and Jorra Vail gives the house no name for them and does not say the room was cold; he comes through with fine grey slate dust worked into both forearms past the bend of his little finger, not the bone-coloured slip of the wheel, and the boy keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray without asking which slate was broken or whether it was a birth-slate. The broken birth-slates stay under the lowest rack, gone around and entered by nobody. Jorra speaks to the wheel before anyone --- it does not care whose hands, only if they are steady --- tells a pot You'll do, knows the full note of a Vail pot before it leaves the wheel and will not say so before a kiln-master from High Kiln who would call it early and make something of it. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper ahead of her sentence, the iron taking the cold out of his fingertip, so the end of her instruction arrives at the pot and the household straightens around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted. He reads the damper once more as the bite that holds a vessel whole and can take the hand off a man, with no word in Grathic for both mercies, and keeps the reading filed as an object, exact and worth nothing, joined to no kiln. Advances T035/T031, T062, T076/T036, T061/T082, T058/T079, T071/T072 (105). Withheld: no name for the men, no opening of the back room, no seventh hearing, no ending.

scenes.title: The Road He Does Not Turn Along
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry continued, Day 105, Seed 16, afternoon at the yard well and in the Clay Yard; going of the light under the roof. Tarn takes the broom only after Sella Vail has given it its instruction and says Yes, house to the ones who want the thaw early and the ones who want it late, agreeing so entirely that no argument can find a foot, and keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went. His chest has been tight since the dark; the small bench knife lies on its sill with six years counted in a mark his thumb has worn almost flat and the seventh nearly gone and still held, the one entry in this house the house cannot check, and to the kindling he says Six counted. The next I don't count. Ash is worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifts it; the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holds what light there is and gives it back. His broom goes over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector, over and over, without once turning along it; he was sent once in the Long Cold, came back at the frozen ford and told the house it had been done, and keeps that sentence where he keeps the seventh year and enters neither. A loan that can hear is a loan that can be called, and the sentence that would call it is never said under this roof. No collector comes. Something must give at the end of the seventh year; it does not give here and the held breath presses to its edge. Dusk under the roof: the file is unchanged, one stiff crust in the fold, the new grey unswept, the two sounds in two places. Advances T036/T076, T009, T088, T061/T082, T062, T071/T072 (105). Withheld: no seventh year spent, no collector sentence entered, no ending.

scenes.title: The Board Beside Hers
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry, Day 106, Seed 17, Seventhday, dawn market at the Fishstairs below the north bridge; a short turn three doors down in House Silt at midday; going of the light under the Vail roof. Sella Vail sets the basket at the end of the fish-trade shade where no slate lies and gives the instruction to the wool and the water and never to the basket. Mira Silt works the eels with pale slime dried on her sleeves and silt dried pale in the hollow of her neck, her head held a little to the right where the top of her left ear had been, her small smile kept like a door on the latch; asked whether the run will be thin she answers her own answer, Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river, and moves eel-bones against her thumb while deciding whether to lie. When a buyer named a figure her thumb goes under her apron to the grey cord and stays, and shifting a creel shows the second cord twisted twice beneath it, never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted and the knot for the thin child upriver untouched. Her board lies beside Orra Weir's knot-string and does not touch it; Orra watches from where she watches and gets no answer. The steps come back four, four and a landing a hand's breadth out of line that a whole market walks over carefully without a fall; the soft-cuffed clerk still sits with his cuff grey from washing and his slate to his forearm for a measure nobody called, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, filed apart from Marra, the Drawing collector and the Court-table clerk, with no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand. Advances T059/T025/T024, T090/T080, T083, T071/T072 (106), T058/T079. Withheld: no knot counted, no word forty, no sixth sighting, no sale.

scenes.title: One Hundred and Six
scenes.synopsis: One dated entry continued, Day 106, Seed 17, midday in House Silt and the walk back up the Clay Yard; afternoon and going of the light under the Vail kiln-house roof. Three doors down Alda Reed lays her birth-slates writing-down on the bench before she turns to the fold, presses the wool a breath too long, crosses two fingers at the red edge of the birth-flower before she knows it and covers the sign with the date she gave Dessa, says Warm and breathing, that's all I've set down, exact and not true, and touches the little tin in her bodice without opening it; her sixth narrow slate stays face-down toward a floorboard in a house the boy cannot name, six pages unread, no seventh written and T023 not paid again. The mercy-lie has curdled through to a fact in a dead woman's face nobody alive can correct. Sella sets the basket just inside the finger's-width-open door away from every open slate, opens no slate and turns no errand into a walk to Slate Row, and carries him home at the half-pace saying nothing about the writing, the tin or the fold pressed too long. Under the roof the boy checks the private file the way a man turns out instruments on a towel and finds it unchanged: six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, three intervals on another tray, the word forty unspoken with the readable double turn beside it, four low things in four places with the river's note a fifth, the two tellings of the shut counting room joined to no kiln with no third, the damper's double bite filed as an object and the loan uncalled. On the loaf shelf in the next room the row keeps its two unnamed gaps and in the fold one brown-edged crust lies stiff with its empty place unnamed and no third; no collector came for the woman in the brook and the morning came all the same. Sella tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot and feeds it; the fire answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and six days. Final image: the door a finger's width open, the river's low muttered note through the gap from the Ilm and the kiln's four, four and a gap through the floor in two separate places, the boards overhead keeping four nails and four and a fifth that is a knot the width of a thumb, and his hand outside the wool going up an inch toward the note of water going over water and coming down; the count at a hundred and six, unspent. Advances T023/T089, T007/T008/T073, T060/T086, T061/T082, T009/T013, T088, T058/T079, T071/T072 (106). Withheld: no tin or box opened, no recognition of the mother, no silt-leach, no joining, no ending.
